title: canonical_pill — unsourced-imperative canonicalization detector
intent: Surface unsourced imperative prohibitions in canonical governance/spec Markdown — permanent-sounding rules (NEVER, MUST NOT, LOCKED) with no citation anywhere in their section. The failure mode is a descriptive observation frozen into permanent law, locking out a still-developmental capability. The detector surfaces candidates for human triage; it does not rule on them.

scope.out_of_scope_notes: No existing analyzer logic or golden fixture is touched, and no governance document in this repo is edited (the detector reads docs, it does not write them). baselines/main.json is deliberately unchanged — the patch adds zero structural debt. The CODE form of over-strict canonicalization (extra="forbid" schemas, frozen invariants) is the same class but a separate, deliberately unbuilt detector.

what_changed: New CanonicalPillAnalyzer (rule CANON_PILL_001) scanning **/*.md and .mdx via its own pruned walk, with three tells: PRIMARY unsourced imperative (uppercase prohibition token in a section carrying no citation), SECONDARY present-indicative-as-law (absence/negation declarative in a prescriptive section), TERTIARY intra-doc contradiction (opposing permission token) attached as contradiction_refs metadata only
Citation adjacency is SECTION-scoped: a citation anywhere between the enclosing heading and the next heading of equal-or-higher level covers every prohibition in that section
Prohibition tokens match case-sensitively on the uppercase form, so casual lowercase prose ('we never got around to X') is silent with no section logic
PRIMARY additionally requires canonical register — a prescriptive heading or a doc-level governance status marker — so ordinary README prose does not become noise
Registered AnalyzerType.CANONICAL_PILL and CanonicalPillAnalyzer in api._DEFAULT_ANALYZERS; refreshed confidence golden/policy and logic manifests (enum-closure only, no version-anchor bump)
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: This is the third observed instance of the over-strict-canonicalization class (RMOS extra="forbid", the CBSP21 freeze-gate, the IBG NEVERs) and the first mechanical surfacing of it. No existing analyzer reads Markdown at all — the runner's `files` list is Python-only — so the governance-prose surface was entirely unexamined. The detector encodes the one mechanical test the IBG audit applied by hand: does the prohibition cite an authority, or is it an unsourced imperative?

commands_run: CI=true PYTHONPATH=<clone>/src py -3.11 -m code_audit debt snapshot . --ci --out <tmp>/current.json
test_results: Ruff clean on both new files

Structural debt snapshot is fingerprint-identical to baselines/main.json (255 items, 0 new, 0 resolved) — an 8-parameter _finding() was refactored to a _Candidate parameter object rather than banking the debt
Manifest refresh is enum-closure only: confidence_logic_version and signal_logic_version both unchanged
Acceptance, FIRES arm (real IBG_ROLE_DEFINITION.md): all four unsourced NEVER rows, the 'No feedback loop exists upstream' declarative, and the footer restatement all fire — 11 candidates total

Acceptance, SILENT arm (the calibration that matters most): 'IBG math is LOCKED' stays silent because its section cites Sevy and Mottola and a ±0.01in tolerance; the tolerance row stays silent; lowercase prose 'never' stays silent; an ordinary README MUST NOT stays silent

Full suite (py-3.11, Windows): 2 failures, both in tests/test_cli_api_parity_js_ts_flagged.py, PROVEN PRE-EXISTING by re-running that module on clean main with this work stashed — identical 'TypeError: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not NoneType' at json.loads(r1.stdout). These CLI-parity tests shell out to the editable install (code-analysis-tool-fresh), whose human summary prints an em-dash that fails cp1252 stdout decoding, leaving proc.stdout None. Not a findings-parity mismatch and not caused by adding an analyzer to the default set. tests/test_api_cli_parity_ci.py fails the same way on clean main and was excluded from the run.
verification.notes: Two interface anchors were verified against the live tree before coding, and one differed materially from the order. (1) `files` is Python-only — core/runner.py:58 is `files = files_by_lang['py']` — so no .md ever reaches an analyzer through it; this analyzer collects its own inputs via a pruned os.walk, following the cross_copy_drift._candidates precedent. (2) Finding/Location/make_fingerprint match the order, but `context_confirmed` is NOT a model field — it is a metadata key, following the single precedent at analyzers/context_pinned_hash.py:287. DEVIATION FROM ORDER, flagged for owner ruling: the order specifies a MEDIUM/HIGH severity ladder, but Severity.HIGH maps to exit code 3 (fail) under the default exit-code policy, which would make a CANDIDATE lead fail a build and contradicts the order's own leads-not-verdicts requirement. Suite severity is therefore capped at LOW (the hollow_guarantee 1.0.0 advisory precedent) and the MEDIUM/HIGH ladder is carried by `confidence` (0.5/0.7) and `metadata.candidate_strength`. This is a one-constant revert if the owner wants literal severities. SECOND DEVIATION: the order lists bare `is`/`exists` as SECONDARY tells; implemented as absence/negation declaratives only, because firing on every `is` in a governance doc floods the output and defeats the register gate. SELF-SCAN (stop condition): 2 candidates in this repo's own docs — .github/copilot-instructions.md:532 and DEVELOPER_HANDOFF.md:517 — both weak SECONDARY hits on 'does/do not <verb>', neither a real poison pill. Recorded, NOT fixed, per the order's no-inline-bundling rule. DOGFOOD FINDING that changed the code: scanning the real luthiers-toolbox docs/governance corpus (88 docs, 107 candidates) showed BLUEPRINT_READER_PROTECTION_RULES.md's Protected Systems table firing, though the order places it in the KEEP arm — its rows cite pinned commit SHAs rather than prose refs. A pinned commit is the strongest form of the 'version pin' citation the order names, so SHA recognition was added (requires both a digit and a hex letter, so 'deadbeef' and '12345678' do not qualify); that table went silent and the IBG arms were unaffected.
